disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set in regulation and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) before hunting or trapping. Trapping in Quebec is governed by the Loi sur la conservation et la mise en valeur de la faune (chapter C-61.1), the Reglement sur le piegeage et le commerce des fourrures (C-61.1, r. 21) and the Reglement sur les activites de piegeage et le commerce des fourrures (C-61.1, r. 3). The authoritative texts are published in FRENCH; the French text governs. This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of Opossum Foot; it is NOT part of the US app, which stays US-only and untouched.

license_summary.certified_traps: AIHTS-certified implements are required for the type/species combinations in Note 2 to Schedule II of C-61.1, r. 21; the ministry publishes the certified trap lists ('Listes des pièges certifiés'). See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.course: Certificat du chasseur ou du piegeur with code 'P' (trapper certificate) is mandatory for a Quebec RESIDENT to obtain a professional trapping licence (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 4(2)). To earn it: be at least 12 years old, complete the training on trapping and fur-bearing animal management ('formation sur le piegeage et la gestion des animaux a fourrure') given by associations affiliated with the Federation des trappeurs gestionnaires du Quebec (FTGQ), and pass the examination. The certificate is permanent and bears code P (quebec.ca, 'Obtenir un certificat du piegeur', updated August 4, 2026).
license_summary.exclusive_rights_leases: On territories where exclusive trapping rights have been granted (territoires reserves aux seules fins de piegeage, zones d'exploitation controlee (zecs), wildlife reserves, outfitter territories), a trapper must hold a bail de droits exclusifs de piegeage (exclusive trapping rights lease) or carry the lease holder's written authorization under s. 96 of the Act (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 10.2). Leases are allocated by draw to residents 18+ holding the trapper certificate; term is 9 years, automatically renewable (C-61.1, r. 3, ss. 14-15); rent is $2.22/km2 per year (indexed; minimum $22.20) (r. 3, s. 16, amounts as indexed). A lease holder must trade at least 15 undressed pelts of at least 5 fur-bearing species from the leased territory each year (10 pelts / 3 species if the territory is 20 km2 or less) with a licensed fur dealer (r. 3, s. 17).
license_summary.fees: 2026-2027 SALE PRICES (quebec.ca, 'Acheter et partager un permis de piegeage', updated August 19, 2026; taxes and the contribution to the Fondation pour la biodiversite et la faune du Quebec included): professional trapping licence - resident $37.40, non-resident $470.48; replacement licence $7.15. The underlying droits in the Reglement sur la tarification reliee a l'exploitation de la faune (C-61.1, r. 32, s. 4, indexed April 1, 2025) are resident $29.38 and non-resident $399.03. Trapper certificate droits were $2.48 under r. 32, s. 1.1 (indexed April 1, 2025); a draft amendment published in the Gazette officielle (December 24, 2025) proposed abolishing certificate droits from April 1, 2026 - enactment not confirmed in this pass (see known_gaps).
license_summary.fur_trade_and_reporting: When trading an undressed pelt of a hunted or trapped fur-bearing animal, the professional licence holder must declare the number of the UGAF the fur comes from (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 10.3). Licensed fur dealers (permis de commercant de fourrures) must keep the minister's numbered purchase register recording, for each purchase: date, number of pelts per species, and the trapper's name, address, date of birth, hunter/trapper certificate number and the UGAF (or hunting zone) of origin; register copies go to the minister by September 10 each year (r. 21, s. 19.2). No general season-end harvest report by the trapper was found in r. 21 or r. 3 - the register system is dealer-side (contrast Ontario's trapper-filed Season-End Harvest Report).
license_summary.harvest_limits: Black bear is the only species with a harvest limit (limite de prise) in the current regulation: maximum 4 per year per professional licence, apportioned by UGAF groups (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 17). The Canada lynx and bobcat limits that appeared in earlier versions of s. 17 are revoked in the current French consolidation (subparagraphs 3-7 'abrogé') - see verification.known_gaps.
license_summary.indigenous_exclusivity_and_north: Indigenous trappers hold exclusive trapping rights in UGAFs 6, 7 (except the La Verendrye wildlife reserve), 29, 31, 32, 50, 56 and 87-96 (MFFP). In northern Quebec, beaver reserves (reserves de castor, Reglement sur les reserves de castor, C-61.1, r. 28) are divided into family lots held under collective exclusive Indigenous trapping rights, and the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement territory (Loi sur les droits de chasse et de pêche dans les territoires de la baie James et du Nouveau-Québec, chapter D-13.1, s. 23) overlays Category I/II/III lands and registered trapping grounds (terrains de piegeage enregistres). The professional-licence/UGAF model in this dataset does not govern Indigenous harvesting under the agreements.
license_summary.licence_sharing: The professional licence may be shared: a spouse, children under 18, and students aged 18-24 may trap using the holder's licence under the conditions of C-61.1, r. 3, ss. 5-7 (under-18s must be accompanied by the holder or spouse for licence use under s. 5; residents among them must hold and carry their own code-P certificate; animals they capture count against the holder's licence and limits). The licence must be carried at all times while trapping (quebec.ca).
license_summary.licence_types: Permis de piegeage professionnel (professional trapping licence) for resident or for non-resident (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 3). A person may hold only one professional trapping licence (s. 7). The licence is valid from its date of issue to the following July 1 and includes 4 transport coupons (coupons de transport) bearing the licence number (s. 3). A Quebec resident is a person domiciled in Quebec for at least 183 days in the year preceding the activity or the certificate application (quebec.ca).
license_summary.nonresident: A non-resident licence holder may trap ONLY on their own private land, or on the territory described in the exclusive trapping rights lease of an outfitter licence holder or a professional trapping licence holder (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 10.1). Non-resident applicants must be at least 12 years old (s. 4(3)); the code-P certificate requirement in s. 4(2) applies to residents.
license_summary.permission: Trap only where authorized: on open (zone libre) public land and private land as permitted, and on exclusive-rights territories only with a lease or the lease holder's authorization document carried on the person (s. 10.2). Trapping is prohibited outright in the small territories shown in Schedules IV-XIII and XV of r. 21, and in the Beauharnois canal territory (Schedule XIV) from the third Saturday of September (September 19, 2026) to December 26.
license_summary.registration_black_bear: A trapped black bear must be identified BEFORE it is moved, using a transport coupon issued with the licence: the coupon's unique number is written indelibly on the animal or on an attached support, and the animal must stay identified until skinning (and until dressing if the pelt is destined for dressing) (C-61.1, r. 3, s. 11, as amended by D. 561-2026). The bear must then be REGISTERED (enregistrement) with the minister or an authorized registration agent, on the minister's form, within 15 days of the bear leaving the trapping site (r. 3, s. 13).
license_summary.report_violation: SOS Braconnage - Urgence faune sauvage: 1-800-463-2191 (24 hours a day, 365 days a year); email centralesos@environnement.gouv.qc.ca; online reporting form on quebec.ca. Regulation information line: 1-877-346-6763; renseignements.faune@environnement.gouv.qc.ca.
license_summary.trap_check: No general trap-check (visit) interval for professional trapping is prescribed in C-61.1, r. 21 or C-61.1, r. 3 as read in this pass (the former obligation sections of r. 3, ss. 9, 10 and 12, are revoked). This is a negative finding, not a verified absence - see verification.known_gaps.
license_summary.trapping_licence: A professional trapping licence is required to trap any fur-bearing animal in Quebec (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 3). There is no general/amateur trapping licence: Quebec trapping is a professional-licence regime. Licence purchase is through 'Mon dossier chasse et peche' or a licence sales agent (quebec.ca).

species.notes: French name: Carcajou. CLOSED. Schedule II of C-61.1, r. 21 permits NO trapping implement for wolverine ('aucun engin n'est permis'), so there is no trapping season. Wolverine is designated a threatened species (espece menacee) under Quebec's Loi sur les especes menacees ou vulnerables (chapter E-12.01; Règlement sur les espèces fauniques menacées ou vulnérables et leurs habitats, E-12.01, r. 2). A fur dealer who comes into possession of a wolverine pelt taken in Quebec outside the Cree/Inuit/Naskapi agreement territory must notify a wildlife protection officer without delay (r. 21, s. 19.2(4)(c)). Do not trap.

verification.confirmation_notes: Trapping periods: the MFFP 'Periodes de piegeage' page (quebec.ca, updated November 25, 2025) was read in full in French and presents the periods set by Schedule III of the Reglement sur le piegeage et le commerce des fourrures (C-61.1, r. 21); the official English version was cross-checked and agrees (one extraction ambiguity on the UGAF 68 canid row was resolved in favour of the French text, which governs: October 18 to March 22). The regulation itself was read in full on LegisQuebec (French): ss. 1-19.3, Schedule 0.1 (species + Latin names), Schedule I (implement types), Schedule II (types per species + Note 2 AIHTS certification), s. 17 (black bear limit; lynx/bobcat paragraphs revoked). The second regulation (C-61.1, r. 3) was read for licence sharing, black bear coupon/registration and lease rules. Fees cross-checked between r. 32 (base droits) and quebec.ca 2026-2027 sale prices. Hunting rows verified in the official 'Periodes de chasse au petit gibier 2026-2028' (generated November 13, 2026), French with English cross-check. Calendar checks: the only relative date in the instruments, the Beauharnois canal closure from the third Saturday of September, computes to September 19, 2026 (verified by calendar); all Schedule III periods are fixed calendar dates, and 2026-2027 dates were assigned with fall openings in 2026 and winter/spring closings in 2027 (black bear spring window: May 15-June 30, 2027). Wolverine's threatened designation verified on the official quebec.ca list (updated March 31, 2025) and E-12.01, r. 2. SOS Braconnage 1-800-463-2191 verified on quebec.ca.
known_gaps: Schedule III's table body did not extract from the LegisQuebec HTML of C-61.1, r. 21 in this session; the periods in this dataset are the ministry's official 'Periodes de piegeage' presentation of Schedule III (updated November 25, 2025). Before the clone launches, diff the dataset name-by-name against the Schedule III table in the official PDF/Gazette version of r. 21.

Canada lynx and bobcat harvest limits: point-in-time English versions of r. 21 (2014/2015) show s. 17 limits (max 7 Canada lynx per year apportioned by UGAF; max 1 bobcat per year). In the current French consolidation read in this pass, s. 17 covers black bear only and its subparagraphs 3-7 are marked revoked ('abrogé'). The dataset follows the current French text (French governs), but this should be re-confirmed with the MELCCFP before launch because older ministry material still circulates with the lynx limit.

Trap-check interval: no general visit/check interval for professional trapping was found in C-61.1, r. 21 or C-61.1, r. 3 (r. 3 ss. 9, 10 and 12 are revoked). Live-capture (capture vivante) rules, municipal bylaws, zec/reserve rules or animal-welfare law may impose visit duties that were not covered; confirm with the MELCCFP before the clone states any trap-check rule for Quebec.

UGAF 67 appears in NO Schedule III period table read in this pass, and UGAFs 87-96 (northern, Indigenous-exclusive) have no published periods in the MFFP table; UGAF 69 has no beaver/river otter period. Whether these are closed, unallocated, or governed by the northern regime is unconfirmed - the dataset simply has no rows for them.

Red fox small-game HUNTING season (Règlement sur la chasse, by hunting zone) exists but its 2026-27 table was only partially extracted in this session; fox hunting rows are not modelled. The same applies to any other furbearer hunting rows beyond coyote, wolf and raccoon.

Trapper certificate fee: r. 32, s. 1.1 set certificate droits at $2.48 (indexed April 1, 2025), but a draft amendment published in the Gazette officielle on December 24, 2025 proposed abolishing certificate droits from April 1, 2026. Whether the amendment was enacted was not confirmed in this pass.

FTGQ training course duration and course fee are not stated on the official quebec.ca certificate page read in this pass (the course is delivered by FTGQ-affiliated associations); not recorded rather than guessed.

The 'Regles generales pour les adeptes de piegeage' page (quebec.ca) was only partially extracted (accordion layout); its 'Limites de prise' and 'Moyens autorises' sections were not read in full. Limits in this dataset come from the regulation text, which governs.

UGAF boundaries: the dataset references UGAF groups only. The 96 UGAFs' boundaries (MFFP publishes UGAF maps per species group) are a separate dataset task, not scoped here. Hunting rows use the separate zones de chasse system, whose boundaries are likewise not in this pass.

Timezone: the dataset uses America/Toronto (Eastern Time, observed throughout Quebec's trapping territory; the Iles-de-la-Madeleine observe Atlantic Time but no UGAF period row in the table is specific to them).

Polar bear: the dataset records the provincial position (no implement permitted, no Schedule III period). Harvest in Nunavik under the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement / Inuit rights regime, including any quota or tagging specifics, was not researched in this pass.

aihts.certification_source: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - 'Listes des pieges certifies' published on the ministry website (referenced in Note 2 to Schedule II of C-61.1, r. 21); the underlying national list is the Fur Institute of Canada certified-trap list (updated July 22, 2026).
aihts.models_note: This pass captured the certification STRUCTURE (which implement types must be certified for which species, per Note 2 to Schedule II), not the model-by-model certified trap list. Certification is not the same as current manufacturing: several certified models are legacy/discontinued. Do not present the certified list as a shopping list without a retailer-availability check.
no_certified_trap_required: Coyote (killing sets; certified traps required for LIVE capture from the 2028-2029 period, per the ministry's three-year notice)
aihts.note: Quebec implements the AIHTS (Accord sur les normes internationales de piegeage sans cruaute / Agreement on International Humane Trapping Standards, D. 116-2000) differently from Ontario: instead of a schedule of certified trap MODELS in the regulation, Schedule I of C-61.1, r. 21 defines nine implement TYPES, Schedule II assigns permitted types to each species, and Note 2 to Schedule II requires specified type/species combinations to be certified as conforming to the AIHTS. The operative certified-model lists are published by the ministry ('Listes des pieges certifies'). Three-year notice (quebec.ca, March 31, 2026): certified traps will be required for the live capture of raccoon from the 2027-2028 trapping period and of coyote from the 2028-2029 period.
trap_rules: Only the implement types listed in Schedule II for a species may be used for that species (C-61.1, r. 21, s. 12(3)). Schedule I defines types 1-9: type 1 = quick-kill spring trap with un-toothed jaws; type 2 = locking neck snare (quick-kill); type 3 = live-holding foot-hold spring trap; type 4 = foot-hold trap or snare rigged for drowning; type 5 = foot snare (lacets) with locking device; type 6 = foot-hold trap with anti-self-mutilation device rigged for drowning; type 7 = underwater cage (cage sous-marine); type 8 = live-holding foot-hold trap with padded/offset/laminated jaws (min 9 mm); type 9 = live-capture cage or box (max 122 cm x 46 cm).

Type 1 implements for long-tailed weasel, least weasel, beaver, ermine, river otter, Canada lynx, bobcat, American marten, fisher, muskrat and raccoon; type 3 for raccoon; type 4 for muskrat; types 3 and 5 for Canada lynx and bobcat; types 5 and 8 for wolf; and type 9 for beaver must be AIHTS-certified (Schedule II, Note 2).

Black bear: type 5 foot snare only per Schedule II, plus a type 2 snare is permitted except from May 15 to June 30 (s. 12). Food bait for black bear is prohibited July 1-August 15 (UGAFs 6, 38-40, 50, 56-66) and July 1-August 31 (UGAFs 1-5, 7-37, 41-49, 51-55, 70-86).
Type 2, 3, 5 and 8 implements must be set so the trapped animal can never be left suspended without support (s. 12).

Muskrat and American mink may also be trapped with a type 7 underwater cage from the species' opening date in each UGAF until December 31; type 7 is prohibited from January 1 to May 15 (s. 14). Inside a muskrat house only type 1 and 6 implements may be placed (Schedule II, Note 1).

A licence holder may use a firearm to dispatch a trapped black bear, lynx, wolf, fox, raccoon, coyote, beaver or striped skunk (s. 16). Trapping may be practised at night (quebec.ca, Regles generales).
NO general trap-check (visit) interval is prescribed in C-61.1, r. 21 or C-61.1, r. 3 as read in this pass - see verification.known_gaps.

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]
aihts.jurisdiction_specific: AIHTS traps now required for live capture of raccoon in cages/boxes; certified coyote live-capture (restraining) traps mandatory as of the 2028-2029 trapping periods. Quebec is also a FIC Note 1 province for raccoon restraining traps. [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: No legally required maximum check interval found - the Regulation respecting trapping and the fur trade (C-61.1, r. 21) was read in full (ss. 1-19.3) and contains no visit/check provision; ministry material says only 'visit regularly'.
check_interval.killing: Same - no interval in the regulation (r. 21 and r. 3 read in full).
check_interval.note: Confidence: not found after searching named sources (R2 Item 1). App should show 'no statutory check interval - visit regularly', not a number.

canada_only.tenure: Leases granting exclusive trapping rights on designated territories (conditional on an annual minimum harvest), plus open trapping by management unit (UGAF).
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: None found - no trap owner-ID marking requirement in the sources searched (follow-up pass, Nov 17); identification runs through licence/tenure and pelt seals instead.
canada_only.royalty: 5% of the Quebec average value per species (Bulletin Fourrure Quebec), owed by licensed fur traders for each raw pelt bought or obtained from a hunter or trapper (Regulation respecting fees relating to wildlife, C-61.1 r. 32, s. 13); traders keep a royalty register and remit monthly. Verified in regulation text. [R2 Item 5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: No NWCO-style licence found. C-61.1 s. 67: a person, or anyone lending him assistance, may capture, move or kill an animal attacking him or damaging his property if it cannot be frightened off (duties under s. 68: release unharmed live animals, declare wounded/dead animals). Whether PAID assistance under s. 67 is expressly sanctioned is not stated in the sources - unconfirmed. SEG permits (scientific/educational/management) are the ministerial authorization route. [R2 Item 3]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: Black bear must be registered within 15 days of leaving the trapping ground, with a transportation coupon attached before the animal is moved; sale of a raw bear pelt requires proof of registration. Polar bear export needs registration proof plus tag number. [R1 s.5]
